description: Fig. 11 is a schematic composite figure (no data axes) arranged as two horizontal rows separated by a blue left-to-right arrow labelled "Increasing Strain" in red text. The upper row, titled "B2-free alloy", contains panels (a)-(d); the lower row, titled "LDS with coarse B2 stringers", contains panels (e)-(h). All panels share one visual vocabulary defined by the legend at right: κ-carbide (small red marker), B2 (olive-green coarse stringer block and fine green dots), Crack (short red line), Austenite (hexagonal grain outline), Annealing twins (double blue lines), Slip band (cross-hatched fill), Strain accumulation (solid green fill) and Deformation twin (brown line). (a) shows austenite grains with a few annealing twins and fine κ-carbides; (b) adds scattered dislocation-pinning symbols; (c) adds cross-hatched slip bands; (d) shows heavily cross-hatched refined slip bands. (e) shows κ-carbides in γ-grains plus a vertical B2 stringer crossing several grains with sparse fine B2 on boundaries; (f) labels 'f' (favourable) and 'nf' (non-favourable) B2 regions with dislocation symbols; (g) adds slip bands and deformation twins; (h) additionally shows a red crack in the B2 stringer. No numeric values, axes or scale bars are printed.

subfigures.description: Initial microstructure of the B2-free alloy (28Mn0Ni): hexagonal austenite grains with a few annealing twins (double blue lines) and fine κ-carbides (small red markers); no B2.
Low strain near yield in the B2-free alloy: same γ grains with annealing twins plus dispersed dislocation/planar-glide symbols within the grains.
Intermediate strain in the B2-free alloy: cross-hatched slip bands initiated within γ-grains, interacting with annealing twin boundaries.
Fracture stage of the B2-free alloy: denser, refined cross-hatched slip bands throughout the grains.

Initial microstructure of the B2-containing alloy (15Mn5Ni): κ-carbides inside γ-grains, a vertical coarse B2 stringer connected across several γ-grains, and sparse fine B2 (green dots) along grain boundaries.

Low strain near yield in the B2-containing alloy: dislocation symbols in γ-grains; a coarse B2 stringer with regions labelled 'f' (favourable OR) showing slip transfer and 'nf' (non-favourable) showing dislocation pile-up at the γ/B2 interface.

Intermediate strain in the B2-containing alloy: slip band formation (cross-hatch) in γ-grains, deformation twins (brown lines) and dislocation interaction with coarse κ-carbides and pile-up near fine B2.
Fracture stage of the B2-containing alloy: inhomogeneous/refined slip bands across grains and a red crack symbol within the green B2 stringer.

observations.observation: The figure is a schematic in two horizontal rows: the top row is titled 'B2-free alloy' (panels a-d) and the bottom row is titled 'LDS with coarse B2 stringers' (panels e-h).
A blue arrow between the two rows, labelled 'Increasing Strain' in red text, points left to right, indicating the deformation sequence across each row.
The right-hand legend defines nine symbols: κ (carbide), B2, Crack, Austenite, Annealing twins, Slip band, Strain accumulation and Deformation twin.
Panels (a) and (e) are the initial microstructures of the 28Mn0Ni and 15Mn5Ni alloys, respectively (caption).
(b, f), (c, g) and (d, h) correspond to low strain near yield, intermediate strain and fracture, respectively (caption).
The letters 'f' and 'nf' printed in panel (f) represent favourable and non-favourable orientation relationship of B2 with γ, respectively.
The initial microstructure of the B2-free 28Mn0Ni after hot rolling consists of austenite grains with a few annealing twins and fine κ-carbides (Fig. 11a).
Panel (e) represents κ-carbides within γ-grains, B2 stringers connected across several γ-grains, and sparse fine B2 along grain boundaries in hot-rolled 15Mn5Ni.
When tensile deformed, the B2-free alloy exhibits planar dislocation glide and pinning (Fig. 11b).

In the B2-containing alloy, grains with a favourable orientation relationship ('f') undergo slip transfer across the γ/B2 interfaces, while non-favourable/hard B2 grains ('nf') show dislocation pile-up at the γ/B2 interfaces (Fig. 11f).
With progressive deformation the B2-free alloy shows slip band initiation within γ-grains along with slip-twin interaction across annealing twin boundaries (Fig. 11c).

The γ-grains in the B2-containing alloy exhibit slip band formation and deformation twinning, with dislocation interaction with coarse near-cuboidal κ-carbides by particle shearing and pile-up near fine B2 particles (Fig. 11g).

The B2-free alloy (d) shows slip band refinement and saturation of mean slip band spacing, while the B2-forming alloy (h) shows inhomogeneous slip band refinement and cracking of B2 at higher strains.
A short red crack symbol is drawn inside the green B2 stringer in panel (h), consistent with cracking of B2 at high strains.
